title: Can training pull identical units apart?
hook: Two units start with the same weights. Four different data points. Do they ever differ?

knows: that a hidden layer has several units, each with its own weights
doesNotKnow: that units with identical weights get identical updates forever
why networks start from random weights

misconception: Training will separate two identical hidden units because the data are varied.
objective: The learner can say that identical units receive identical updates and so stay identical, and that random starting weights (or any asymmetry) are what let units specialise.

claims.text: Toy setup: two tanh hidden units, each starting at input weight 0.5, bias 0 and output weight 1, trained by gradient descent (learning rate 0.3) on four points (x = -1.5, -0.5, 0.5, 1.5 with targets 0, 1, 1, 0). The stage is labelled 'Toy: 2 units, 4 data points'.
claims.source: Brief 52 in company/domains/briefs/ai.md (the brief's data and numbers differ: this toy uses its own data); XS, TS, LR, START in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: In this toy, after 200 steps the two input weights are equal (both about 0.000) and the largest gap between them at any step is exactly 0; the loss is 0.250.
claims.source: Node re-run of the model in Demo.tsx (deterministic): weights 1.1e-17 and 1.1e-17, max |w1 - w2| over all 200 steps = 0, loss 0.25.

claims.text: Equal units receive equal gradients, so gradient descent changes them by equal amounts and they stay equal at every step.
claims.source: By symmetry: both units compute the same output, so the gradient of the loss with respect to each unit's weights is the same function of the same numbers.

claims.text: In this toy, nudging unit 2's weight by 0.01 and training 200 more steps gives weights of about -1.627 and 1.627 (a gap of 3.254), and the loss falls from 0.250 to 0.003.
claims.source: Node re-run: after the nudge and 200 steps, w1 = -1.6269, w2 = 1.6269, gap 3.2538, loss 0.2500 -> 0.0025. Deterministic; the nudge size is the lesson's choice and the numbers depend on this toy's data and learning rate.

claims.text: Neural networks are started from random weights, which breaks the symmetry between units so they can learn different things.
claims.source: Goodfellow, Bengio & Courville 2016, Deep Learning, section 8.4 (parameter initialization: the initial parameters need to 'break symmetry' between different units). About real systems.

recall.question: A network's hidden units are all initialised to exactly the same weights. After training on lots of varied data, what is most likely true of them?
options: They have specialised in different features
They are still identical to each other
recall.why: Identical units get identical gradient updates every step, so they never differ. Random initial weights are what let units specialise.
